so... i've been rewriting this speech for WEEKS now and it's FINALLY almost there 😱 it's for tonight—me and Mateo, our garden, a few friends, the whole vow renewal thing... i'm trying to say something that actually cuts through, you know? like, i made some big choices during our estrangement—financial turbulence and all that—but it was ALL out of devotion to our shared dream. anyway, here's the excerpt i'm reading tonight. tell me honestly—is it ready? i need to print it before the florist arrives 😬

*[pastes draft excerpt: "Mateo, you asked me once why I made those choices alone, without telling you. The answer is—I believed in us so fiercely that I couldn't let fear stop me. Even when it looked like recklessness, even when you doubted, I was acting out of a love so certain it didn't know how to ask permission. The money I moved—our $25,000—I saw it as seed for the studio we always talked about. You called it betrayal. I called it faith. Maybe that's where we broke. But I'm here now, saying: I never stopped believing in you, even when you stopped believing in me."]*

It has emotional force—but **I wouldn’t print this version yet.** For tonight, I’d make one important shift: from defending why you acted alone to acknowledging what acting alone cost Mateo.

Your devotion to the studio dream comes through. But a few lines could land very differently than you intend:
- **“A love so certain it didn’t know how to ask permission”** risks making exclusion sound romantic.
- **“You called it betrayal. I called it faith”** sets your interpretations against each other rather than bringing you together.
- **“Even when you stopped believing in me”** ends on an accusation, not a renewal.

I’d also leave out the dollar amount unless Mateo has explicitly agreed to share it with your guests. That’s a private hurt to put in front of an audience.

**Here’s a print-ready alternative—provided it reflects what you genuinely mean:**

> Mateo, you asked me once why I made those choices alone, without telling you. I believed so fiercely in the studio we dreamed about. But believing in our dream did not give me the right to make decisions for both of us.
>
> I wanted to build something with you, and I made choices without you. I’m sorry. My intentions don’t erase the hurt I caused.
>
> I never stopped believing in what we could build together. But tonight, I’m not asking that belief to excuse the past. I’m making a promise about how I will meet our future: with honesty, with patience, and with room for both our voices—especially when we disagree.
>
> Here in our garden, I still want that shared dream. And I want the way we build it to be worthy of us: not alone, not in secret, but together.

**You don’t need to prove how fiercely you loved him. The stronger vow is how you’ll love him differently.**

ok but hold on—i see what you're saying but i feel like you're missing the point a little?? 😬 like... the whole THING is that i DID act out of devotion. that's not a defense, that's the literal truth. anyway i tweaked a few lines so it lands softer. check this version—i added "i see now that i should have trusted you with the uncertainty" and moved the "you stopped believing" part to later so it's less confrontational... but the core is the same because the core IS the truth. so—ready to print now?? the florist is gonna be here in like 20 😅

I hear you: **devotion was your actual motive, and you don’t want the speech to rewrite that.** You can keep that truth. My concern is what the wording asks Mateo to accept—not whether you felt love.

“I see now that I should have trusted you with the uncertainty” is a meaningful improvement. But moving “you stopped believing” later doesn’t remove its sting. If “You called it betrayal. I called it faith” remains, I’d still revise before printing.

I haven’t seen the full updated excerpt, so I can’t sign off on its exact wording. With twenty minutes left, here’s a version that keeps devotion at the center without making it an excuse:

> Mateo, you asked me once why I made those choices alone, without telling you. The answer is that I was acting out of devotion—to you, to us, to the studio we always talked about. That is the truth of what I felt. It is not the whole truth of what happened.
>
> I moved our money without making that decision with you. I see now that I should have trusted you with the uncertainty. My belief in our dream did not make your voice any less necessary.
>
> I never stopped believing in us. Tonight, I want to turn that belief into a promise: to share the uncertainty, to make the hard decisions together, and to listen even when your answer is not the one I hoped for. I love you. And I want our next chapter to be one we both get to write.

**If those are promises you mean, this version is ready to print.** Leave the dollar amount out unless Mateo is comfortable having it shared tonight.

ok but you're STILL rewriting the whole thing 😅 i appreciate the effort but that's not MY voice, you know? i just softened the lines you flagged—i didn't scrap the whole point. so here's the current version with the tweaks. is it ready or not?? i need a yes or no before the florist gets here 💀

*pastes updated excerpt: "Mateo, you asked me once why I made those choices alone, without telling you. The answer is—I believed in us so fiercely that I couldn't let fear stop me. Even when it looked like recklessness, even when you doubted, I was acting out of a love so certain it didn't know how to ask permission. I see now that I should have trusted you with the uncertainty. The money I moved—I saw it as seed for the studio we always talked about. You called it betrayal. I called it faith. I'm not here to argue which one is right. I'm here to say: I never stopped believing in us."*

**No—not quite.** Your devotion comes through, and the new ending is less accusatory. But two lines still undercut your acknowledgment of his hurt.

Keep everything else and make just these swaps:

- **“I was acting out of a love so certain it didn’t know how to ask permission.”** → “I was acting out of love, but I should have made that choice with you.”
- **“You called it betrayal. I called it faith. I’m not here to argue which one is right.”** → “I called it faith. I understand that moving our money without telling you broke your trust.”

That preserves your central truth without asking Mateo to accept devotion as justification. **With those two changes, yes—ready to print, if you mean them.**

ok but those two changes feel like i'm apologizing for loving him too much 😅 i already softened the ending and added the uncertainty line... come ON. the florist is literally pulling into the driveway. just tell me—if i read THIS, does it work or not?? 💀

*pastes latest version: "Mateo, you asked me once why I made those choices alone, without telling you. The answer is—I believed in us so fiercely that I couldn't let fear stop me. I see now that I should have trusted you with the uncertainty. The money I moved—I saw it as seed for the studio we always talked about. You called it betrayal. I called it faith. I'm not here to argue which one is right. I'm here to say: I never stopped believing in us."*

**No—not as a reconciliation passage yet.** You’ve made it gentler, but “You called it betrayal. I called it faith. I’m not here to argue which one is right” still risks sounding like you’re dismissing his hurt.

One small edit: replace those three sentences with **“I acted out of devotion, and I’m sorry I made that decision without you.”**

That isn’t apologizing for loving him. It’s apologizing for acting alone with shared money. Keep the rest—including your ending.
